previous_description: End result intended or already achieved by the organization or a system, distinct from a Goal which expresses the desired direction.
definition: A motivation element stating a concrete, preferably measurable end result that the organization or a system has achieved or intends to achieve, usually with a target value, threshold or time frame. It describes a state that can be checked as reached or not reached, not a direction of intent or a capability the system must provide.

distinguish_from.when: the statement expresses a desired direction or end state without a measurable target or verifiable completion point (e.g. 'improve customer satisfaction')
the statement specifies what a system or solution must do or exhibit (a need to be realized by design), rather than the business or system result that follows from it
the element expresses the worth or utility to a stakeholder (e.g. 'lower operating cost'), not the concrete result that produces that worth
the statement records a finding about the current state of affairs (a SWOT item, risk or gap) rather than an intended or achieved result

code_evidence: A key result or success criterion in an OKR, roadmap or epic document stating a measurable target with a date, e.g. 'checkout abandonment below 20% by Q4'
A 'Success metrics' or 'Expected outcome' section in a PRD, RFC or ADR describing the verifiable result after delivery, often tagged with a tracking status such as done, on-track or at-risk
An SLO or KPI objective in monitoring or dashboard configuration (e.g. a Datadog/Prometheus SLO target) whose name and description reference a business result and link to a stated goal

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text statement of the result, including the measure, target value or threshold, and target date where known; set it for every outcome so its achievement can be verified.

notes: No attributes for measure, targetValue or targetDate, so measurability lives only in free text; consider adding them. Both 'influence' and 'realizes' to goal exist; ArchiMate standardizes realization. Outcome 'realizes' value is non-standard; ArchiMate associates value with outcome. SLO targets overlap with apm metric elements; the outcome is the target, not the instrument.
